html:
On the Marchfeld plain northeast of Vienna, on 26 August 1278, Rudolf of Habsburg, king of Germany, defeated and killed King Ottokar II of Bohemia. It was one of the largest battles of knights in medieval Europe.

Ottokar had taken Austria and Styria after the Babenberg dukes died out, and built a realm stretching from Bohemia to the Adriatic. Rudolf, a minor Swiss count elected king in 1273, demanded the lands back. With Hungarian allies he won the battle, helped by a reserve of knights he held back until the end.

Rudolf gave Austria to his sons in 1282. It became the heartland of the House of Habsburg, which ruled from Vienna for more than six centuries, until the end of Austria-Hungary in 1918. It followed the Privilegium Minus that made Austria a duchy. See Austria.
